To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reasons given for withdrawal from college vary greatly depending on the type of withdrawal.

(1) students who are dismissed from college report more severe academic and personal problems than do students who transfer to other colleges or those who leave college voluntarily, (2) students who leave college during a semester do so for different reasons than do those who leave at the end of the year, and (3) there is little relationship between class standing at the time of withdrawl and the reasons for withdrawal.

(a) students who withdraw voluntarily from college are more likely to report problems than are transfers or dismissals, (b) students who withdraw during the semester are more likely to have academic problems than are those who withdraw at the end of the year, and (c) students who withdraw at the beginning of the academic year are more likely to be experiencing academic problems than are students who withdraw at any other time during the academic year.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reasons given by students who have withdrawn from college, and with the characteristics of the students who withdraw.
the reasons why students withdraw from college and with the problems they encounter.
the problem of identifying and classifying reasons for college withdrawal, and with the relationship of these reasons to other factors.

the reasons given for leaving college by different subgroups of withdraw als are quite different.
there is no single reason why students drop out of college.
there is a great deal of variation in reasons for withdrawal, and that the most important factors in the decision to withdraw are not the same for every student.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more severe the problems, the more likely the student is to be academically dismissed rather than to transfer or to leave voluntarily.
students who withdraw from college have many different reasons for doing so.
students who withdraw are a very heterogeneous group and that the problems they report differ considerably from those of students who stay in school.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many different reasons for leaving college, and that it is important to distinguish between different subgroups of students who drop out.
students are not leaving for the reasons we think they are, and that the reasons they are leaving are different for different subgroups.
the reasons given for withdrawal from college may be more a function of the subgroup of students who are leaving than of the reasons why they are leaving.
